title: Head of Hardware
description:
Accelerating embodied AGI. 

The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.

MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.

We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.

Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Head of Hardware, you own that hardware end to end: electrical, firmware, and the mechanical integration that holds it together, from the first schematic to devices running on factory floors.

You lead the team that builds it. Today that is about six engineers on robotics, three on EMG sensing, and three on camera systems, plus contractors, and it will grow quickly. Our Electrical Engineer and Embedded Engineer roles report to you. You set the architecture they build against, and you still build alongside them.

This is a founder-shaped role, not a management seat. We are looking for someone who has carried a product from a blank page to customers with real skin in the game, wants to build both the thing and the team that builds it, and would rather design than review. If that sounds like you, you will want to do it again at the earliest stage.

What You Will Do

- Own the hardware roadmap for Shift and Atlas data capture: wearables, sensor rigs, camera systems, and prototype robots. What we build, in what order, and why.

- Set the system architecture across electrical, firmware, and mechanical: sensors, compute, power, wireless, and enclosures. Make the trade-offs, and make them stick when disciplines disagree.

- Stay on the bench: schematics, layout reviews, board bring-up, and a scope in your hands when the team is stuck. On the days it matters, you are the best electrical engineer in the room.

- Lead and grow the team: hire, set the bar, run design reviews, and give engineers ownership of whole subsystems rather than tickets.

- Guarantee data quality end to end: EMG and EEG front ends, camera pipelines, IMUs, and synchronization across many devices, so that what reaches the ML team is clean, time-aligned, and trustworthy.

- Take designs from prototype to small-batch production: DFM, component and EMS vendors, test fixtures, certification, and field reliability.

- Work shoulder to shoulder with ML and deployment. Your hardware decides what the training data looks like, and you will be on the floor where it is captured.

- Run contractors and partners without losing ownership of the result.

Requirements

- You have taken at least one product from zero to shipped, with significant ownership of the outcome: as a co-founder, CTO, first hardware hire, or the lead who owned the whole device. Not one subsystem, not one phase. Ideally a wearable, at a tier-one hardware company known for shipping at scale.

- Electrical engineering is your home discipline. You have designed boards that shipped, across mixed-signal, power, wireless, and high-speed digital, and you can still do it today.

- You think in systems. You understand how an electrode choice, an enclosure tolerance, and an ADC sample rate interact, and you can hold the mechanical and firmware conversations as a peer, not a customer.

- You have led engineers: hired them, grown them, and kept a team shipping through 0-to-1 ambiguity. Typically 6+ years in hardware, but we care more about what you shipped than how long it took.

- A strong understanding of how hardware decisions affect data quality. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you design accordingly.

- Experience taking hardware to small-batch production: DFM, vendor and EMS management, test, and certification.

- Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice.

- High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. A 0-to-1 hardware program takes the hours it takes, in person and at pace, and you have chosen that before.

- Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care.

Nice to Have

- Wearables, smartwatches, drones, robotics, AR/VR, or defense wearables on your résumé.

- Camera systems: sensor selection, MIPI and ISP pipelines, and multi-camera synchronization.

- Low-power and battery design, BLE or Wi-Fi, and antenna integration in small enclosures.

- Enough mechanical fluency (CAD, tolerances, and materials) to challenge the mechanical team’s choices and be right some of the time.

- Prior founder or founding-engineer experience, including the parts that went wrong.

- Open-source hardware or firmware contributions.

Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI

Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:

- Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it.

- Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.

- Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.

- Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.

This is for you if: 

- You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec.

- You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one.

- You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do.

This is not for you if: 

- You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5.

- You would forward output you cannot explain.

- "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer.

How We Hire

We read every application and reply within five working days.

- Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways.

- Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes.

- Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it.

- Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO.

- Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem.

Then a decision, usually within a few days.

Pay Transparency

Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting.

What We Offer

- Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter.

- Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval.

- A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage.

- Free food and drinks in the office.

Equal Opportunity

MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity.

Job Overview Solactive's Aggregate team owns the intraday calculation of our indices: consuming live price streams, applying calculation logic across a wide range of indices, and producing a continuous output stream of index ticks throughout the trading day. The core platform is built in Java and engineered around throughput, latency, and correctness under concurrency, while custom business integrations are built in Python. - Help investigate correctness or performance issues: reproduce them, narrow them down, and propose fixes with senior guidance
- Build and maintain Python integrations for business teams: connectors to the calculation platform, output adapters, validation checks, and small operational tools
- Contribute to monitoring and developer tooling that makes calculation behaviour observable and easier to reason about

- Openness to Python: no prior experience needed, but willingness to pick it up for integration and tooling work alongside Java
- Familiarity with Git, the command line, and a testing mindset; interest in measuring performance rather than guessing at it
- Ability to work independently on a scoped task, ask for help early when stuck, and communicate clearly in writing
- Available for 15–20 hours per week during the semester, more during semester breaks
- Interest in financial markets, market data, or index calculation is welcome but not required

title: Senior Industrial Designer | Robotics
description:
Your tasks - Shape the hardware identity: Define how our humanoids look and feel: proportions, surfaces, overall silhouette. You take the design direction we already have and carry it through to physical systems that actually ship.
- Design for passive safety first: Safety sits in the geometry from the first sketch. You work through clearances, pinch points, contact surfaces and fall behavior so the robot is safe around people before software gets involved.
- Integrate complex systems: Package the internals (sensors, cameras, cooling, connectors, cable routing) so the technical parts look intended.
- Physical human machine interaction: Design status signals, touchpoints and small physical cues that tell the people working next to the robot what it is doing and what comes next.
- Build the ecosystem around the robot: Extend the design language to charging docks, transport cases, maintenance gear and packaging.
- From model to CAD: You build physical models fast, see what holds up, and change them until they do. Then you do the surfacing and hand over CAD that engineering can build from directly.
- Materials and processes: Select finishes, review physical samples, and work suppliers on feasibility, cost and lead times. You are willing to try materials that are not standard and to bring in specialized external labs.

Your profile - Background: A degree in industrial or product design, or an engineering degree where the design side is clearly the stronger half.
- Experience: Around five years or more designing physical products, in house or at a studio. Robotics, medical devices, lab and industrial equipment, mobility, or another field where the hardware has to hold up in front of people.
- Small series: You have worked on products built in the hundreds rather than the millions, and know how much that changes what a shape can be.
- Safety and regulation: You have designed under mechanical safety requirements before, so guarding, clearances and contact safety are familiar territory rather than a new topic.
- Tools: Surface modeling in Rhino, Onshape, SolidWorks or Fusion, plus 3D printing and enough workshop practice to build your own models.
- Working with engineers: You read mechanical drawings, keep up in technical discussions, and can explain why a design decision matters.
- Languages: Fluent English. German is nice to have, not a requirement.

Why us? - Ownership from day one: The physical design and hardware identity of our humanoids is yours. Short decisions, no approval chains, and you work directly with the founders and lead engineers.
- Everything under one roof: Labs, workshop and test rigs are in the same Kreuzberg building. The engineer you need is a walk away, not a ticket.
- Room to get better: Paid learning time and a personal budget for it, projects where something is allowed to not work the first time, and support for portfolio work and conference talks as the company becomes known.
- Benefits: A benefits package you put together yourself, covering mobility, home setup, health or food. Plus one extra paid day off a year for volunteering or a project you care about.
How to Apply 

Send us your portfolio and a few lines about one product you took from sketch to production : what changed along the way, and why. No cover letter needed. 

Process : Intro call -> Portfolio deep-dive with the founders -> Half-day on-site visit with a small design exercise -> Offer.

We build robots for everyone, so we want a team that reflects that. We hire on what you can do, and we welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in hardware design. If you don't tick every box but think this is your job, apply anyway.

title: (Senior) Manager Projects & Process Excellence (m/w/d)
description:
First things first Hamburg · Vollzeit · Befristet auf 2 Jahre 

Als ( Senior) Manager Projects & Process Excellence (m/w/d) übernimmst du Verantwortung für strategische Veränderungs-, Effizienz- und Softwareprojekte – von der Analyse bis zur Umsetzung. Du strukturierst komplexe Themen, entwickelst belastbare Projektpläne und behältst Meilensteine, Ressourcen, Risiken und Abhängigkeiten im Blick. Dabei bringst du die unterschiedlichen Fachbereiche und das Management zusammen, bereitest klare Entscheidungsgrundlagen vor und steuerst klassische, agile und hybride Projekte . Du bist die Schnittstelle zwischen den Anfordernden aus den Fachabteilungen und dem Technology-Team, entwickelst Prozesse sowie unsere Projekts tandards weiter und sorgst dafür, dass aus Konzepten konkrete, messbare Verbesserungen werden. Projektmanagement ist bei uns mehr als Koordination und Administration. 

Deine Aufgaben Deine Kernaufgaben sind: 

- Strategische Projekte leiten:  Du leitest eigenverantwortlich bereichsübergreifende Veränderungs-, Effizienz- und Prozessoptimierungsprojekte sowie Software- und Digitalisierungsprojekte.
- Agile Softwareprojekte steuern : Du arbeitest eng mit Fachbereichen und Entwicklungsteams zusammen, koordinierst Prioritäten und Abhängigkeiten und hilfst, die agile Zusammenarbeit weiter auszubauen.
- Komplexität in umsetzbare Pläne übersetzen:   Du klärst Ziele und Umfang, strukturierst Arbeitspakete und steuerst Meilensteine, Zeit, Ressourcen, Budgets, Risiken und Abhängigkeiten: klassisch, agil oder hybrid.
- Entscheidungen vorbereiten und vertreten:  Du erstellst entscheidungsreife Management-Updates und Steering-Unterlagen mit Empfehlungen, Szenarien und klaren Entscheidungsbedarfen. Projektergebnisse und Zielkonflikte vertrittst du souverän gegenüber Stakeholdern und Führungskräften.
- Teams zusammenbringen:  Du führst interdisziplinäre Projektteams lateral und moderierst Workshops und Entscheidungsprozesse – dabei bringst du unterschiedliche Perspektiven und Prioritäten zusammen. 
- Energiewirtschaftliche Projekte voranbringen:   Du arbeitest dich in die relevanten Zusammenhänge im Umfeld von Energiehandel, Direktvermarktung und digitalen Lösungen ein, stellst die richtigen Fragen und führst fachliche, technische und operative Anforderungen zu belastbaren Lösungen und konkreten Projektergebnissen zusammen.
- End-to-End-Prozesse verbessern:  Du analysierst Abläufe, erkennst Brüche und Verbesserungspotenziale und gestaltest wirksame, effiziente Prozesse mit klaren Verantwortlichkeiten und pragmatischen Lösungen.
- Budgetcontrolling:  Du prüfst projektbezogene Stunden und Kosten, koordinierst die Rechnungsfreigabe und behältst das Projektbudget im Blick.
Darüber hinaus gestaltest du unser Projektmanagement weiter: 

- Verbesserungen wirklich umsetzen:   Du treibst die gemeinsam identifizierten und beschlossenen Effizienz- und Prozessverbesserungen voran und überprüfst, ob die angestrebte Wirkung im Alltag eintritt.
- Projektmanagement weiterentwickeln:  Du entwickelst Methoden, Frameworks und Best-Practices weiter, besonders für agile Softwareentwicklungsprojekte, und stärkst damit Qualität, Tempo und Ergebnisorientierung.
- Projektarbeit bereichsübergreifend verankern: Du bindest die relevanten Fachbereiche ein, integrierst die Projektarbeit in den laufenden Geschäftsbetrieb und sorgst für klare Verantwortlichkeiten, verbindliche Entscheidungen und sichtbare Fortschritte. In einer Organisation mit dezentralen Zuständigkeiten entwickelst du unsere Projektmanagement-Strukturen, Rollen und Standards pragmatisch weiter.

Dein Profil Das bringst du mit: 

- Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der eigenständigen Leitung komplexer Projekte, idealerweise in Veränderungsprojekten, Prozessoptimierung, Digitalisierung oder Softwareentwicklung.
- Fundierte Praxis im klassischen Projektmanagement, zum Beispiel in Planung und Steuerung von Umfang, Terminen, Ressourcen, Risiken und Abhängigkeiten.
- Vor allem bringst du praktische Erfahrung im agilen Projektmanagement von Softwareentwicklungsprojekten mit und hast idealerweise bereits KI-gestützte Werkzeuge oder Methoden im Projektkontext eingesetzt.
- Erfahrung darin, fachliche Anforderungen mit technischen Teams zu klären und aus komplexen Fragestellungen umsetzbare Arbeitspakete und Entscheidungen zu machen.
- Klare Kommunikation, analytisches und strukturiertes Denken sowie die Fähigkeit, auch bei unterschiedlichen Perspektiven und Prioritäten Orientierung zu schaffen.
- Sicherheit in der Moderation von Workshops und in der lateralen Führung interdisziplinärer Teams.
- Interesse daran, Projektmanagement-Strukturen, Rollen und Standards weiterzuentwickeln. Du bringst Eigeninitiative, Pragmatismus und den Anspruch mit, Konzepte nicht nur zu entwickeln, sondern Ergebnisse gemeinsam mit den Beteiligten in die Praxis zu bringen.
- Ein abgeschlossenes Studium oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation. Entscheidend ist für uns vor allem deine relevante Projekterfahrung.
- Erfahrung in der Modellierung und Dokumentation von Geschäftsprozessen mit BPMN sowie deren Anwendung im Projektmanagement. 
- Energiewirtschaftliche Erfahrung ist ein Plus, aber keine Voraussetzung. Hilfreich sind Kenntnisse zu erneuerbaren Energien, Direktvermarktung, Stromhandel, Bilanzkreismanagement, PPAs oder virtuellen Kraftwerken. Du solltest jedoch bereit und in der Lage sein, dich zügig in energiewirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge einzuarbeiten, fachliche Anforderungen zu verstehen und gemeinsam mit den Teams in tragfähige Lösungen und umsetzbare Arbeitspakete zu übersetzen.

Warum wir? Als wachsendes Unternehmen im Bereich erneuerbare Energien und Energiehandel mit Start-up-Atmosphäre bieten wir dir nicht nur ein vielseitiges Aufgabenfeld, sondern auch echten Gestaltungsspielraum, Verantwortung und die Möglichkeit, aktiv an der Energiewende mitzuwirken. title: Senior Sales Manager UK
description:
Our project for you: moebel.de is Europe's leading price comparison site for furniture and home furnishings. Our family of portals operates in nine European countries, including Germany, France, Spain, the Netherlands, Italy and Poland.

Now we are getting started in earnest in the UK: living24.uk is live – our price comparison site for furniture, home furnishings, garden and décor, as well as white goods and home electronics. The launch is done, the technology works. What decides the pace now are the retailers: the more relevant shops list their ranges on living24.uk, the stronger the comparison for users – and the faster the portal grows.

This is not selling from a tidy list of existing accounts. You take on a freshly launched market and build the partner portfolio that living24.uk runs on. Whoever delivers over the next few months will shape what moebel.de looks like in the UK.

That is why we are looking for you as Senior Sales Manager UK.

Your future Tasks - Building the market: you build living24.uk's partner portfolio – from first contact through pitch and negotiation to the signed contract. Your targets are UK online retailers in furniture, home furnishings, garden, décor, white goods, home electronics and small appliances.
- Selling a performance model: you show retailers how living24.uk pays off as an additional channel – through cost per click, visibility, feed quality and cost-of-sale.
- Seeing partners through to go-live: product feed, tracking, range checks – together with the team in Hamburg. After go-live our Relationship Management team takes over day-to-day care, so you can focus on winning new partners.
- Presence in the market: retailer visits, trade fairs and industry events across the UK. In a young market, trust is built face to face.
- Ear to the ground: competition, price levels, what UK retailers expect, seasonality – what you learn in the field feeds into product, pricing and priorities.

Your Strenghts - Several years of sales experience in UK e-commerce, ideally with a price comparison site, marketplace, affiliate network or performance marketing provider
- A solid network of UK retailers in our categories that you can put to work from day one
- Command of the performance model: CPC, CPO, affiliate, product feeds, ROAS and cost-of-sale are selling points for you, not buzzwords
- A hunter's mindset: you keep your own pipeline full, cold outreach included, and get deals over the line
- An appetite for building: pace and open questions appeal to you more than a field that has already been ploughed
- Working from the numbers, with clean CRM records as the basis for how you steer
- Willingness to travel across the UK and to regular meetings in Hamburg
- Fluent English at negotiation level – German is a plus, not a requirement

Our Benefits Your day is yours to shape 

Work when you are most productive. Early bird or night owl: you set your hours flexibly, in agreement with your team. Working from another European country for a while? No problem. Your laptop is your workplace.

Our culture is one of a kind 

Here everyone sits on the same couch, regardless of title or role. We live team spirit online and in person – gaming nights, workouts, film evenings and team events.

Four times a year we meet for Company Week 

Working together in the office, pushing projects forward, pizza evenings and a party to finish.

In the heart of Hamburg 

When you are in Hamburg, our office is waiting for you – centrally located between the main station, Mönckebergstraße and the Binnenalster lake. Perfect for lunch dates, a break by the Alster or a stroll after work.

We are looking forward to receiving your application! Please send your application exclusively through our online application form – it goes straight to our recruiting team. You are welcome to submit your CV in English or German, ideally with your salary expectations and earliest possible start date.

title: Senior Sales Manager Polen (m/w/d)
description:
Unser Projekt für Dich: moebel.de ist Europas führender Preisvergleich für Möbel und Einrichtung. Mit unserer Portalfamilie sind wir in neun europäischen Ländern aktiv, darunter Deutschland, Frankreich, Spanien, die Niederlande und Italien.
Jetzt legen wir in Polen richtig los: mobi24.pl ist live – unser Preisvergleich für Möbel, Einrichtung, Garten und Dekoration sowie Weiße Ware und Haushaltselektronik. Der Launch ist geschafft, die Technik läuft. Über das Tempo entscheiden jetzt die Händler: Je mehr relevante Shops mit ihren Sortimenten auf mobi24.pl vertreten sind, desto stärker der Vergleich für die Nutzer und desto schneller wächst das Portal.
Das ist kein Vertrieb aus einer gepflegten Bestandsliste. Du übernimmst einen frisch gestarteten Markt und baust das Partnerportfolio auf, das mobi24.pl trägt. Wer hier in den nächsten Monaten liefert, prägt, wie moebel.de in Polen aussieht.
Dafür suchen wir dich als Senior Sales Manager Polen (m/w/d).

Deine zukünftigen Aufgaben - Marktaufbau: Du baust das Partnerportfolio von mobi24.pl auf – vom Erstkontakt über Pitch und Verhandlung bis zum Vertrag. Zielgruppe sind polnische Online-Händler aus Möbel, Einrichtung, Garten, Dekoration, Weiße Ware, Haushaltselektronik und Elektrokleingeräte.
- Performance-Modell verkaufen: Du erklärst Händlern, wie sich mobi24.pl als zusätzlicher Kanal rechnet – über Klickpreise, Sichtbarkeit, Feed-Qualität und Kosten-Umsatz-Relation.
- Bis zum Livegang begleiten: Produktdatenfeed, Tracking, Sortimentsprüfung – gemeinsam mit dem Team in Hamburg. Danach übernimmt unser Relationship Management die laufende Betreuung, du konzentrierst dich auf neue Partner.
- Präsenz im Markt: Händlerbesuche, Messen und Branchenevents innerhalb Polens. In einem jungen Markt entsteht Vertrauen im persönlichen Gespräch.
- Ohr im Markt: Wettbewerb, Preisniveau, Erwartungen polnische Händler, Saisonalitäten – deine Erkenntnisse fließen in Produkt, Pricing und Priorisierung ein.

Deine Stärken - Mehrjährige Vertriebserfahrung im polnische E-Commerce, idealerweise bei Preisvergleich, Marktplatz, Affiliate-Netzwerk oder Performance-Marketing-Anbieter
- Ein belastbares Netzwerk zu polnische Händlern aus unseren Kategorien, das du ab Tag eins nutzt
- Sicherheit im Performance-Modell: CPC, CPO, Affiliate, Produktdatenfeeds, ROAS und KUR sind für dich Argumente, keine Buzzwords
- Hunter-Mentalität: Du hältst deine Pipeline eigenständig voll, auch per Kaltakquise, und bringst Abschlüsse über die Linie
- Lust auf Aufbauarbeit: Tempo und offene Fragen reizen dich mehr als ein fertig bestelltes Feld
- Zahlenbasiertes Arbeiten und saubere CRM-Pflege als Grundlage deiner Steuerung
- Reisebereitschaft innerhalb Polens und für regelmäßige Termine in Hamburg
- Polnisch verhandlungssicher, Englisch sicher im Arbeitsalltag – Deutsch ist ein Plus, keine Voraussetzung 

Unser Angebot Dein Tagesablauf gehört dir 

Arbeite dann, wenn du am produktivsten bist. Ob Früh- oder Spätaufsteher: Bei uns passt du deine Arbeitszeiten flexibel an – in enger Abstimmung mit deinem Team. Zeitweise Arbeiten aus dem europäischen Ausland? Kein Problem. Dein Laptop ist dein Arbeitsplatz.

Unsere Kultur ist einmalig 

Hier sitzen alle auf derselben Couch – unabhängig von Titel oder Rolle. Teamspirit leben wir digital und vor Ort, z. B. bei Gaming Nights, Workouts, Filmabenden oder Teamevents.

Viermal im Jahr treffen wir uns zur Company Week 

Gemeinsam im Büro arbeiten, Projekte pushen, Pizzabende genießen und mit einer Party abschließen.

Mitten in Hamburg 

Bei deinen Aufenthalten in Hamburg erwartet dich unser Büro zentral zwischen Hauptbahnhof, Mönckebergstraße und Binnenalster – perfekt für Lunch-Dates, Pausen an der Alster oder einen Feierabendbummel.

title: Account Executive
description:
Account Executive

Festanstellung, Vollzeit · Berlin (HQ)

Deine Mission

Die Energiekosten in Europa sind doppelt so hoch wie in den USA und China. Gleichzeitig wird sich die Stromnachfrage bis 2050 voraussichtlich verdoppeln. Marktpreisvolatilität und zunehmende Komplexität werden uns erhalten bleiben. Damit steht das Rückgrat der europäischen Industrie unter Druck – und Unternehmen müssen jetzt handeln.

trawa entwickelt die Lösung: die erste integrierte B2B-Energieplattform, die Energiebeschaffung, Energiemanagement und die Steuerung von Flexibilitäten in einem Produkt vereint. Supply, Manage, Flex – kombiniert. Diese Integration ermöglicht Einsparungen von bis zu 30 % bei den wiederkehrenden Stromkosten und unterstützt Unternehmen gleichzeitig dabei, auf erneuerbare Energien umzusteigen.

Wir sind Europas am schnellsten wachsende B2B-Energieplattform. Aktuell sind wir in Deutschland und Österreich aktiv und planen, unsere Aktivitäten 2027 auf einen dritten Markt auszuweiten. Unser Ziel ist die europaweite Skalierung. Wir bewegen uns schnell – das Marktfenster ist offen, und wir wollen es nutzen.

Über trawa

trawa ist ein Scale-up mit Sitz in Berlin und rund 100 Mitarbeitenden, davon etwa 30 in Product & Tech. Bis heute haben wir mehr als 35 Millionen Euro eingesammelt, darunter eine Series-A-Finanzierungsrunde über 24 Millionen Euro im Mai 2025. Zu unseren Investoren zählen Balderton, Headline, Speedinvest, AENU, Magnetic und Tiny VC.

Wir suchen eine:n Account Executive , um gemeinsam die nächste Wachstumsstufe zu erreichen. Du berichtest an unseren Head of Sales und arbeitest eng mit unseren Commercial-Teams zusammen.

Die Position ist in Berlin angesiedelt. trawa ist ein Office-First-Unternehmen : In der Regel arbeitest du an fünf Tagen pro Woche aus unserem Büro.

Das Team

Unser Sales Team ist ein zentraler Bestandteil für den kommerziellen Erfolg von trawa. Vom Erstkontakt mit einem Lead bis zum erfolgreichem Abschluss mit einem Kunden, berät das Team mittelständische Unternehmen zu unseren ganzheitlichen Energielösungen.

Wen wir suchen

- Ermögliche signifikante Stromkosteneinsparungen bei unseren Kunden durch gezielte Positionierung unserer Lösungen zur intelligenten Stromversorgung und Steuerung von Batteriespeichern

- Kommuniziere den Mehrwert unserer Produkte klar und überzeugend, indem du die Anforderungen der Kunden auf kommerzieller und technsicher Ebene verstehst

- Übernimm Verantwortung für Geschäfts- und Pipeline-Ziele: Aktive Steuerung und Erreichung der definierten Umsatz- und Wachstumsziele

- Baue nachhaltige Beziehungen zu Entscheidungsträgern auf und entwickle Accounts eingenständig weiter

- Identifiziere Cross- und Upselling-Potenziale und erweitere das Lösungsspektrum bei bestehenden Kunden

- Arbeite eng mit unserem Vertriebsinnendienst zusammen, um effiziente und reibungslose Vertriebsprozesse zu gewährleisten

Deine Ziele in den ersten 90 Tagen

- Du hast das notwendige Verständnis zu unseren Produkten, zum Energiemarkt, zur Sales Journey unserer Kunden sowie zu relevanten internen Prozessen aufgebaut

- Du hast dich als fester Ansprechpartner für deine Kunden rund um unsere Lösungen etabliert - und berätst sie ganzheitlich und kompetent

- Du hast mehrere Kundenprojekte bereits umfangreich entwickelt, sodass erste vertriebliche Erfolge zeitnah absehbar sind

Was dir zum Erfolg verhilft

- Erfahrungen in der B2B-Kundenkommunikation, z. B. als Account Executive, Account Manager oder im Business Development Bereich

- Erfahrung in der Energiewirtschaft bzw. Erneuerbare Energien ist ein großes Plus, aber kein Muss

title: Head of Operational Integration
description:
About Andercore 

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials for energy, infrastructure, and construction in wholesale and beyond.

We trade with global suppliers and distribute to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade and distribution end-to-end: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, and embedded financing. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier; for our partners, it is the most convenient and safe way to do business across borders. Behind it, our software and agentic AI do the heavy lifting that used to take an asset-intensive supply chain with four or five intermediaries and weeks of manual coordination.

Where we are today:

- Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover

- Seven European markets live

- 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), offices in London, Mumbai, and Shanghai

$40M Series B just closed, $75M raised to date from Atomico, Project A, and Inven Capital, institutional financing from international banks.

We are building the world's first and last industrial-grade AI operating system for materials, redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

Acquisitions are our second growth path. We buy established industrial distribution businesses in the EUR 20-40M revenue range, owners and management stay on board, and we connect them to our platform, our procurement, our financing lines and our AI stack. Three deals are live, two are close to signature, and at run rate we intend to close around five per year out of a mapped universe of roughly 200 targets.

Role Overview

You own what happens after signing.

Origination, valuation and deal execution sit with the CEO and our senior M&A advisor. Your mandate starts the day a company becomes part of Andercore and it ends when that company runs better than it did before.

These are analog businesses. Fifteen years old, owner-led, hemdsärmelig, a well-run P&L and almost no technology underneath it. They are profitable, they are growing, and they are at their operational limit. Our hypothesis is that our platform, our purchasing power, our credit facilities and our automation take them past that limit. Your job is to find out on the ground whether that hypothesis holds, in which order, and at what pace - and then to make it happen with the management team, not to them.

We do not arrive as the saviour with the AI magic box. We say so explicitly to every seller, and you will hold that line.

What You Will Own

Holding Management from Day 1

- Access to accounting and financials from day one, monthly numbers on a fixed close, one reporting framework across all acquired entities.

- Set the baseline: revenue, margin, working capital, cash, customer and supplier concentration. No opinion without the number behind it.

- Pick up the commitments made during due diligence and turn them into the operating rhythm of the first 100 days.

- Run the portfolio as a financial participation first. Both companies are growing. Do not put anything into a skid.

On-the-Ground Diagnosis

- Spend real time inside the acquired businesses and find out where they actually stand, which is never where they say they stand.

- Map the connection points: procurement, pricing, inventory, sales productivity, logistics, financing, ERP, reporting.

- Test our integration theses against reality, quantify the ones that hold, kill the ones that do not, and bring the correction back to the CEO fast.

Value Creation

- Sequence and land the levers with the management team: central procurement, our credit and working-capital facilities, pricing, sales productivity, customer intelligence, automation of manual back office.

- Decide with the CEO what gets centralized, what stays entrepreneurial, and what we take from them - the flow runs in both directions, several of these companies do things better than we do.

- Track every lever against the original investment case in euros.

Owner and Management Relationship

- Be the peer of a Geschäftsführer who built a EUR 30M business himself. Credibility comes from having done operating work, not from a framework.

- Be the one who checks whether things are as good as they are described, and who says it out loud when they are not. The CEO stays the partner; you bring the uncomfortable version.

- Manage expectations in the other direction too: we are not a service provider that solves the acquired company's problems for it.

Playbook and Team

- Codify integration into a repeatable capability: Day-1 checklist, reporting standard, diagnostic framework, lever library, 100-day plan.

- Make the fourth acquisition faster than the first, then build and lead the team that runs them in parallel.

Scope Boundaries / What This Role Is Not

- Not M&A. No origination, no valuation, no LOI, no SPA. That sits with the CEO and our senior M&A advisor.

- Not a PMO. Nobody here sends a 400-line integration plan with traffic lights to an owner-manager. That gets you thrown out of the room, correctly.

- Not a consulting engagement. You are measured on the numbers of the acquired companies, not on the quality of the analysis.

- Not a corporate integration role. These are not hierarchical organizations that execute what the centre decides.

- Not a process you inherit. There is none yet. You build it.

What We Are Looking For

You are an operator out of a private equity value-creation or portfolio operations team, or a generalist from strategy and transformation with real time spent inside operating companies. Roughly eight to twelve years in.

You bring:

- At least one integration or post-close situation you personally carried, where you can name the specific knotty problem you solved and why it worked. We will ask for that story in the first interview.

- Operating substance: you have sat in procurement, pricing, supply chain, finance or sales of a real company, not only next to it.

- Geländegängigkeit. You are comfortable with an entrepreneur who is highly intelligent, rough around the edges, and holds two cars and a boat inside the company. Nothing about that scenario throws you.

- People work as roughly half the job. Influence without formal authority, because these managing directors did not sign up to be managed.

- A strong observer. You read a business and a person quickly and accurately.

- Fluent German and English. German is not optional; these conversations happen in German.

- Fluency with modern AI tooling and the instinct to automate your own work. You do not need to be an engineer.

You do not need five PMI programmes on your CV. We would rather you had none than that you learned to fill in lists instead of thinking.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 12 months:

- Every acquired entity reports monthly on one framework, on a fixed close, with us having access to accounting.

- Each acquisition has its integration thesis validated or killed with numbers within 90 days of closing.

- The acquired businesses keep growing. No customer, supplier or key person lost to the transaction.

- The first value-creation levers are live and their P&L impact is measurable in euros.

- A documented playbook exists, and the next integration starts faster than the last.

Over time you own integration and value creation for the whole group at a pace of several acquisitions per year, and build the team that delivers it.

Package

- Fixed base plus a variable component tied directly to the success of each integration.

- Virtual equity in Andercore at the current strike, with meaningful upside if we build what we intend to build.

- Direct work with the Founder & CEO, the M&A advisor, the Board and our investors.

We are building the world's first and last industrial-grade AI operating system for materials, redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

Role Overview 

As VP Engineering, you own the Engineering organization and turn our platform and AI vision into shipped systems. You report to the Chief Product Officer and partner closely with product, commercial, operations, and finance. You lead our Senior Product Engineers, Staff Engineers and QA, and work closely with our product managers, who own product and design.

This is an execution mandate. You carve our core systems into a modern platform, build our AI agents into one holistic system that runs the trade lifecycle end-to-end, and scale the teams that deliver it. You inherit a working machine at full speed: your job is to rebuild it in flight without losing a day of momentum. In your first year, the priorities are the carve-out of our transaction core and bringing our AI agents into one orchestrating layer.

Key Responsibilities 

AI and Automation 

- Build our AI agents into one holistic, orchestrating AI layer across sourcing, pricing, quoting, sales, logistics, and financing.

- Drive automation of the full transaction lifecycle, and own automation-rate and no-touch-quote targets as first-class delivery KPIs.

- Work with our data team, which sits with the CPO, on systems that make our trade flows a compounding advantage, so every transaction makes the system smarter.

- Keep us at the practical frontier of agentic AI: ship what creates leverage now, skip what is demo-ware.

- Put the guardrails, evals, and human-in-the-loop controls in place so automation stays reliable where it matters most: money-touching and customer-facing paths, where a wrong output is a real loss, not just a bug.

Platform and Architecture 

- Own execution of the target architecture for the Andercore platform, the system of record for industrial trade.

- Lead the carve-out of our transaction core into a modern, modular light ERP (a lean core system for our trade transactions), with a clear migration path and zero disruption to daily trading.

- Shape the role of Salesforce in our landscape: decide what stays on the platform, what moves to the new core, and how the two work together.

- Make pragmatic build-vs-buy calls within the platform strategy and keep technology cost per transaction on a falling curve.

- Make new-market launch a repeatable platform motion: multiple geographies, currencies, languages, and compliance regimes, built in rather than bolted on.

- Keep the platform ready to pass technical due diligence at any moment: architecture, data, and security in shape for the next financing round.

Engineering Organization and Talent 

- Lead the Engineering organization: onsite talent in Berlin and a nearshoring team. Team structure and ways of working stay in-house, and you manage the nearshoring team directly and actively, not at arm's length through a vendor.

- Build lean by default. The goal is not to grow headcount but to build a small, high-leverage team and raise output through AI across the engineering workflow. You lead as an AI-first engineering leader.

- Hire and develop senior engineering leaders, including 1–2 Staff Engineers who report to you and own architecture across teams, and raise the talent bar with every hire.

- Build an engineering culture of ownership, speed, and craftsmanship: small teams, high leverage, no bureaucracy.

- Stay hands-on: review designs with your Staff Engineers, pair on the hardest problems, unblock teams, and keep decisions close to the code.

Enablement and Data Integrity 

- Enable business teams to build and automate with AI safely. Set the paved paths, standards, and review practices that let non-engineers move fast without compromising quality, security, or the systems underneath.

- Partner with the CPO, who owns data, on data integrity: build systems that keep one source of truth with clear access and quality controls, so that faster building never degrades the data the company runs on.

- Make speed and safety one operating model, not a trade-off, and communicate it across the company so every team knows how to move quickly within clear boundaries.

Delivery and Cross-Functional Partnership 

- Act as technical sparring partner to the CPO on architecture, roadmap feasibility, and sequencing.

- Translate the product roadmap into shipped software, and turn front-line needs from commercial and operations into delivery.

- Support the CPO and CEO in technical due diligence with a clear, numbers-backed view of architecture, data, and AI.

- Communicate technical priorities and trade-offs transparently across the company, so everyone understands what we build and why.

What Success Looks Like 

- Engineering operates with clear ownership and no loss of delivery speed.

- Our transaction core runs on a modern, modular platform: the carve-out is live and the migration path is executed.

- One orchestrating AI system increases automation rate and transactions per employee, quarter over quarter.

- Technology cost per transaction falls while volume grows.

- Architecture, systems, and AI stand up to any technical due diligence.

- Hiring runs fast and consistently: senior hires close within six weeks, with one bar across interviewers.

What You Bring 

- Senior engineering leadership at scale, having run and grown multi-team organizations, ideally across more than one location.

- Deep experience with transactional platforms, ERP-style systems, or comparable systems of record, ideally including regulated financial flows such as payments, lending, or KYC, and re-platforming or carve-outs in a live environment.

- Hands-on track record shipping AI or ML in production, with a real sense for where agentic AI creates leverage today.

- A demonstrated AI-first, lean mindset: you have applied AI in your own engineering organization to raise output without growing headcount, not just talked about it.

- Strong architectural judgment, with security and data protection built into your decisions, and enough technical depth to stay close to the code.

- The judgment to know where reliability must be absolute and where speed wins: you move fast on everything reversible and hold a high correctness bar on the irreversible, money-touching paths.

- A plus: a track record of enabling non-engineering teams to build safely with AI, balancing speed

- against quality and data integrity, and the communication skills to carry that across a whole company.

- A plus: comfort in a company where operations come first and software follows, turning manual services into products.

- A commercial mindset: you anchor engineering decisions in unit economics, working capital, and speed for buyers and suppliers.

- A plus: experience with Salesforce as part of a larger system landscape.

Practical details 

- Location: Berlin

- Process: conversations with the CPO, the CEO, Chief of Staff, and members of the engineering team.

description:
About Focused Energy 

Focused Energy is an international deep-tech company based in Germany and the US, working to commercialize laser-driven nuclear fusion. Our mission is to provide clean, safe, and virtually unlimited energy to the world. We are rapidly scaling and looking for talented individuals who thrive in building clarity and structure within fast-growing environments.

Join us as a Principal Control Systems Engineer and help to provide the clean energy of the future. In this role, you will help shape the long-term control systems architecture and technical vision, defining standards and leading the end‑to‑end delivery of critical control systems across our experimental and production environments in Germany and the USA, in collaboration with a passionate, cross‑functional team.

What You’ll Do 

- Design the system‑level architecture for control systems across facilities, making strategic platform and technology choices in collaboration with program and system owners

- Direct real‑time and embedded control solution implementation, selecting and guiding use of PLC, FPGA and other real‑time platforms, balancing performance, reliability, safety and cost trade‑offs

- Work together with system integrators, electrical engineering, cabinet builders, and technicians to specify, design, review, test, install, and commission control cabinet hardware and field devices

- Work together with the software team to architect and deliver fully integrated SCADA, HMI and data systems for alarms, logging, historian, analytics, data reduction, dashboards, etc., ensuring scalability and high performance

- Orchestrate system integration across multiple complex subsystems and teams; define observability, logging and diagnostic strategies and lead root‑cause investigations and post-mortem studies of active systems to deliver lessons learned and contribute to continuous availability improvement

- Shape requirements, documentation and validation approaches at system level, including design specs, interfaces and test strategies for reliability, safety and long‑term maintainability

- Coach and mentor senior and junior engineers, identify capability gaps, grow technical capabilities in key skill areas, and champion best practices for software engineering, testing, quality, and ways of working within the controls team and beyond

Who You Are 

- Degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering, Control/Automation, Mechatronics/Robotics, Physics or similar; PhD or equivalent experience preferred, with recognition as a technical expert in control/embedded or real‑time systems

- Typically 10+ years in control/embedded systems, factory or plant automation, automated test systems, or complex scientific experimental work, with architectural ownership across multiple projects or products

- Deep experience in at least one relevant domain (e.g., high energy lasers, nuclear, robotics, power/energy, automotive, aerospace, industrial automation) with understanding of domain constraints standards and regulations, as well as supplier ecosystems and main players

- Proven track record specifying control cabinet hardware; defining house standards, ensuring compliance with regulations, liaising with system integrators, and creating test plans and quality control processes

- Proven track record specifying control software and/or SCADA and data acquisition systems; defining interfaces, patterns and coding standards across teams, and guiding technology trade‑offs

- Extensive experience with embedded and real‑time platforms (e.g., PLCs in ST IEC 61131‑3, FPGAs, RTOS‑based systems, robotics), including selecting platforms and scaling architectures with clear RAM vs cost/reliability trade‑offs

- Understanding of software/firmware engineering best practices (version control, branching, design for test, CI/CD, automated testing, defensive programming) and experience introducing or improving these practices, and organizing or conducting training programs across teams or organizations

- Excellent communicator (English), able to influence technical direction at organization level, handle and resolve ambiguities in requirements and processes, and build alignment across hardware, software, product and operations teams in hybrid, cross‑site environments

- Practical, hands‑on approach with a strong track record orchestrating large‑scale HW/SW integration, resolving integration challenges, and leading complex debugging and fault‑finding on real systems

- Desirable skills and knowledge (please highlight any of the following in your application):

- Deep experience with PLC programming in ST (IEC 61131‑3); Beckhoff PLCs and TwinCAT system design and architecture, multi-PLC distributed control

- SCADA (especially Ignition) and/or designing and deploying SCADA systems and applying cross-site HMI standards for large-scale and complex systems

- Embedded or real‑time systems (FPGAs, RTOS, microcontrollers, robotics), including platform selection and long‑term maintainability strategies

- LabVIEW architect level (CLA) with focus on FPGA and embedded targets,

- Experience with complex scientific equipment or large‑scale facilities, including diagnostics, vacuum systems, motion platforms and safety interlocks

- Image processing and machine vision, motion control and robotics, high‑precision stepper/piezo systems and encoders

title: (Senior) Technical Partnerships Manager  - Corporate Travel (all genders)
description:
Distribusion is the world’s leading ground transportation marketplace and gives travelers seamless access to ground transportation online, from search to ticket purchase. We have built a cutting-edge B2B technology platform that connects bus, rail, and ferry operators in 70+ countries with the biggest online retailers, including Google Maps and Booking.com .
We are shaping the future of travel and building the largest global network of transport providers and retailers. We are one of the fastest growing startups in travel, backed by leading VCs (TQ Ventures, Lightrock, Creandum and Northzone), and now, following our recent $80m Series C funding, we are ready to push beyond.

Distribusion is quickly expanding globally and looking for a (Senior) Technical Partnerships Manager to join the Corporate Travel Partnerships team to drive the strategic growth and performance of some of our key partnerships in the business travel space. This role will require you to wear many hats and certainly not leave you bored! 

What you will do: 

- Support Pre-Sales: Act as a technical expert during initial engagements to evaluate partner needs and demonstrate our capabilities. 

- Consult on API Implementation: Guide partners through their API integration, ensuring a seamless process that meets certification standards. 

- Translate Requirements: Gather technical requirements directly from external partners and break them down into actionable specs for internal teams. 

- Manage Custom Projects: Drive the end-to-end delivery of custom developments, managing timelines, stakeholders, and go-live execution 

- Guide Product Development: Leverage partner feedback and insights to shape the ongoing development of our core API and integration tools. 

- Manage Technical Relationships: Own the long-term technical relationship with partners to drive collaboration, product engagement, and brand stickiness. 

Workplace: We are mainly looking for this role based in Germany, preferably at our headquarters in Berlin. 
We are a remote-first company, with teams around the Globe and our HQ office in Berlin, where the team often meets in the office. 

Who you are: 

- 5 + years of work experience in a tech company (experience in a technology/software company, travel agency, transportation, and logistics industry is an advantage but not a must). 

- You have had deep exposure to API integrations, and you are confident in navigating documentation, sprint cycles, and system architecture, even if you’re not the one coding. 

- A big plus if you have experience in the corporate travel space (any vertical). 

- You’re a structured communicator who can translate complexity into clarity for both technical and non-technical stakeholders. 

- You take ownership, thrive in ambiguity, and are energised by solving cross-functional coordination challenges. 

- You’re fluent in English, both written and spoken. Other languages are a plus. 

- You’re open to business travel, as needed. 

What you can expect: 

- You will join a fast-paced travel tech company and take on a rapidly growing industry. 

- You will take on ownership and responsibility from day one and have a direct impact on the success of the company. 

- We value agility! We’re constantly updating our tech stack and offer the best possible tools to ensure all of our in-house engineers, partners, and carriers benefit from cutting-edge, efficient solutions. 

- You will work with global companies. Our product attracts the biggest names in travel technology, such as Booking.com, Google Maps, and national carriers like Amtrak, Deutsche Bahn, Renfe, and SNCF. 

- You will join an international team of talented and driven people with a clear mission. Expect your colleagues to inspire, support and challenge you every day! 

- We offer flexible and remote working conditions, relocation opportunities, and career growth in a small and developing company. 

Our hiring process for this role: 

Your Talent Partner (TP) and point of contact is Masha Marynova, and the Hiring Manager (HM) is Sara Fahrenhorst.
For any queries, please reach out to your Talent Partner at ( ). 

Do you want to work in an advanced tech environment and have an impact on millions of travellers around the globe? Come join us!

In this role you own all of finance at Superchat end to end and report directly to the founders. When the board or our investors have a question about the numbers, you're the one who answers it.
You'll take over our financial model and turn it into something the whole company can steer by. You'll own accounting through to the P&L, run forecasting and liquidity planning, and lead the annual audit.

Who We Want 

7+ years of finance experience. 
You know the full cycle first-hand, from closing to forecast to board reporting. 

Closing and audit expertise. 
You independently own monthly and annual closings under HGB, including revenue recognition and accruals, and you coordinate the annual audit with our external auditors through to completed financial statements. 

Expert financial modelling. 
You build driver-based, integrated three-statement models from scratch and you document them so that others can operate them too. 

Forecasting. 
You've owned full budget and forecast cycles, you bring together top-down targets and bottom-up input from team leads, and you treat forecast accuracy as a measurable figure that has to improve. 

Business partner.

Strong communicator.

Manages the status quo. 
You run an inherited function competently, but you don't develop it further. 

Reports instead of advising. 
You deliver numbers without drawing a recommendation from them, and consider the job done once the report is sent.

Looking for predictability.

Your Day To Day 

Financial Model & Steering (~30%)

You'll work alongside our researchers and software engineers: Research explores new approaches, and you turn the ones that work into reliable production systems. In this role, you will:

Agentic Systems

Collaboration

Preferred:

IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. 

Location: Oxford, England
Travel: As needed 
Job ID: 1905

The Role:

We are looking for a Technical Programme Manager to join the Quantum Systems Infrastructure (QSI) team at IonQ's Oxford office. QSI builds and runs the platform our next-generation quantum computers are built, tested, released and operated on, from bare metal in the lab to cloud, working across both Oxford and the US.

Your mission is to run the machinery that keeps QSI’s portfolio visible, planned and unblocked so engineers can engineer, leaders can lead, and the business always knows what is changing and why it matters. You will work very closely with the Technical Programme Managers in the Software and Science teams, ensuring our processes and workflows complement and integrate with their work, rather than duplicating effort. 

We run a centralised PMO operating model at IonQ which you will be a core part of though on a day to day basis you will work alongside the QSI team. As part of this model, this role will not make technical decisions, own engineering headcount, or define product but it will make the programme around those things run.

Responsibilities :

You will own programme execution across QSI’s delivery streams, translating a leadership-visible roadmap into clear plans, measurable milestones and predictable delivery. You will create and run the operating rhythm that keeps teams aligned and leaders informed. When priorities shift, you will implement structure to that ambiguity, clarifying scope, coordinating trade-offs and pushing problems to resolution.

Key responsibilities include:

- Owning programme execution across QSI’s delivery streams: one planning rhythm, one backlog discipline, ensuring dependencies and risks surfaced early and chased to resolution.

- Running the roadmap-to-delivery link: keeping the roadmap, Jira and reality agreeing with each other, and making slippage visible early.

- Owning the programme ceremonies and the design of the workflows behind them (day-to-day stand-ups are run by the engineering managers).

- Working hand-in-hand with the Software and Science TPMs: shared or integrated processes wherever teams interact, and no duplicated ceremonies, boards or reporting.

- Coordinating across teams - Continuing Engineering (US), the PMO, product and science teams - serving as QSI’s cross-functional programme liaison.

- Establishing programme cadences and reporting (changelogs, demos, leadership summaries etc) in plain English that non-infrastructure stakeholders can read and trust.

- Running the intake and triage process so requests reach the right stream with the right priority, without engineers being interrupt-driven.

Requirements: 

We’re looking for a technically fluent Programme Manager who brings structure, pace and clarity to a fast-moving infrastructure organisation. You will be comfortable working in a deeply technical environment, working daily with platform and systems engineers, while translating progress, risks and trade-offs into clear reporting senior stakeholders can trust. You will thrive in ambiguity and an organisation where you are able to drive change. You do not just coordinate: you unblock teams, keep plans honest, and raise the bar on how programmes are run.

You will have prior experience tunning technical programmes across multiple engineering teams, ideally in infrastructure, platform or systems engineering environments. You should be fluent with modern programme tooling, such as Jira, Confluence and GitHub, and have the judgement to keep process lightweight.

title: SEO Manager, EU/UK
description:
ABOUT QUINCE 

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE 

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

- We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.

- Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths. 

- Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory. 

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

Europe is Quince's next growth engine. We have launched in the UK, with further European markets on the roadmap, and organic discovery is one of the biggest untapped levers we have.

We are looking for an SEO Manager, UK & EU. You will own the organic strategy for our European markets across both traditional search and generative engines (AEO), building our European playbook.

This is a cross-market, hands-on role with an unusual amount of ownership. Technical SEO standards and platform-level architecture come primarily from our global SEO team in the US; you are the person who translates those foundations into a European strategy, identifies where Europe needs something different, and makes the case for it. You will work day to day with storefront, copywriting, merchandising, growth marketing, engineering and data — and you will be the main driver for organic growth in the region.

If you want to build an organic program from the ground up in markets where the brand is still being established, this is that job.

What you'll do 

- Own the UK/EU SEO & AEO strategy. Build and maintain a market-level roadmap that reflects the real competitive dynamics of each country rather than a copy of the US plan. Decide where we play, which categories we go after first, and what winning looks like in each market.

- Partner closely with the global SEO team. Adopt and apply global technical standards, feed European requirements into the global roadmap, and flag where a one-size-fits-all approach breaks down in-market.

- Drive answer engine optimisation across Europe. Build Quince's presence in AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and the surfaces that follow. Own structured data coverage, entity and brand consistency, citation-worthy content, and the measurement approach that tells us whether any of it is working.

- Make localisation a search advantage, not an afterthought. Work with copywriting and localisation to ensure category, PDP and editorial content targets genuine local search demand — not translated US keywords. Build the keyword and demand research foundation for each market and turn it into briefs writers can act on.

- Own international search architecture in-market. Hreflang and market targeting, URL and domain structure, canonical logic, indexation of localised catalogues, and the crawl health of each European storefront — specced and QA'd with global SEO and engineering, with you accountable for the outcome.

- Shape the storefront with merchandising and site merch. Influence category taxonomy, navigation, on-site search and PLP structure so that pages serve organic discovery as well as conversion. Partner on how content is modelled in our CMS and how listing pages are built and ranked.

- Work in lockstep with growth marketing. Understand where organic and paid overlap, where they cannibalise, and where organic can take load off paid spend. Bring an incrementality mindset to the way we report and invest.

- Own SEO/AEO readiness for new market launches. Define the checklist, run it, and make sure every new European storefront goes live search-ready rather than being retrofitted six months later.

- Measure, report and build the case for investment. Own market-level organic reporting and the quarterly narrative for European and global leadership.

Required experience 

- 5+ years in SEO, ideally in ecommerce, retail or consumer brands, with meaningful ownership of organic performance.

- Demonstrable experience running SEO across more than one country or language.

- Strong working knowledge of technical SEO: crawl and indexation, site architecture, structured data, page performance. 

- Content-led SEO experience: keyword and demand research, content strategy, briefing writers, and building category and editorial content that ranks and converts.

- Practical exposure to AEO — structured data, entity management, and a real point of view on how Quince should show up in AI-driven discovery.

- Comfortable in the data: Google Search Console, GA4, and the standard SEO toolset (Ahrefs, Semrush, Screaming Frog or similar).

- Excellent communicator in English, and effective working asynchronously with a headquarters team in another time zone.

- A bias for shipping. You are happy operating without a large team, deciding what matters most this quarter, and doing the work yourself.

Preferred 

- Working proficiency in English and, preferably, a second language (e.g. German, French, or Spanish).

- Experience launching ecommerce storefronts in new countries.

- Familiarity with headless CMS and search stacks (e.g. Contentful, Algolia) and translation management platforms (e.g. Smartling).

- Experience using AI-assisted tooling to produce or optimise content, metadata and structured data at scale.

- Apparel, home or lifestyle retail experience in the European market.

Who you are 

- You think in systems. You would rather build a repeatable process that scales to five markets than win one category by hand.

- You are genuinely curious about how discovery is changing, and you are already testing how AI-driven search behaves in your own markets.

- You are persuasive without authority. Much of your impact comes from convincing merchandisers, writers, engineers and a global team to prioritise your work.

- You are commercially minded. You connect organic performance to revenue, not just to rankings.

- You are comfortable with ambiguity and with being early. Europe is not a finished operation, and you will help decide what it becomes.

WHY QUINCE? 

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY 

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

We review all requests individually and will work with you to determine appropriate accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Quince will conduct background checks in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Security Advisory: Beware of Frauds 

At Quince, we're dedicated to recruiting top talent who share our drive for innovation. To safeguard candidates, Quince emphasizes legitimate recruitment practices. title: Senior IT Analyst
description:
About The Role The Senior IT Analyst is the principal in-house resource responsible for day-to-day IT support, providing first and second-line user support and day-to-day IT operations for approximately 80 users. As the principal person responsible for day-to-day IT operations, they will take ownership of incidents and service requests across the support lifecycle rather than operating solely as an escalation resource.

This is a broad, senior analyst role for someone who is technically capable, comfortable working independently and able to manage competing priorities. The postholder will respond directly to users, resolve routine enquiries and requests, investigate more complex issues through to resolution and coordinate external technology suppliers where specialist expertise is needed. Alongside business-as-usual responsibilities, the role will support and deliver smaller technology projects and service improvements.

By keeping FAIRR’s technology secure, reliable and easy to use, the role enables colleagues to focus on delivering FAIRR’s mission with investors and partners worldwide.

Key Outcomes & Accountabilities OUTCOME 1: Users receive dependable, responsive IT support, with issues owned and resolved end to end 
- Act as the principal in-house point of contact for day-to-day IT support, providing both first and second-line assistance according to operational needs.
- Resolve straightforward incidents and requests promptly, while taking the lead on more complex technical issues requiring deeper investigation and second-line expertise.
- Own and manage incidents and service requests from initial contact through to resolution, including access, software, equipment, permissions and non-standard user requirements, coordinating third-party suppliers or specialist support when required.
- Monitor recurring issues, identify root causes and implement practical improvements to reduce repeat incidents.
- Maintain accurate support records and produce clear information on service volumes, performance, trends and user experience.

OUTCOME 2: Joiners, movers and leavers have the right access and equipment at the right time, and no more 
- Coordinate all IT activities for joiners, movers and leavers in collaboration with HR and relevant managers.
- Create, amend and remove user accounts, licences, group memberships, permissions and application access accurately and on time, including removal of leaver access no later than the end of their last working day (or earlier where instructed by P&C).
- Prepare, issue, recover and securely manage laptops, mobile devices, peripherals and other IT equipment.
- Perform periodic access reviews and maintain appropriate evidence of approvals and completed actions.
- Manage shared, service and other non-person accounts, ensuring ownership, purpose and access are recorded.
- Where instructed by P&C or the Senior IT Manager, securely preserve or retrieve account and device data to support subject access requests, investigations or legal matters, maintaining confidentiality throughout.

OUTCOME 3: IT changes are implemented in a controlled way with minimal disruption 
- Plan, assess, document, communicate and implement routine IT changes in a controlled manner.
- Ensure changes have appropriate approvals, testing, implementation steps, back-out arrangements and post-change review where proportionate.
- Maintain the IT change schedule and coordinate activities to minimise disruption to users and business operations.
- Communicate planned changes clearly to affected users and stakeholders.
- Where changes need to take place outside normal working hours, schedule these in advance with the Senior IT Manager’s agreement (see Section 8).

OUTCOME 4: IT services and workplace technology operate reliably and are used effectively and securely 
- Administer Microsoft 365 and other cloud applications used by the organisation, including routine configuration, licence and user administration.
- Support laptops, mobile devices, meeting-room technology, printers, connectivity and standard workplace applications.
- Coordinate hardware repairs, replacements, warranty cases, software renewals and operational supplier activities.
- Maintain user guides, knowledge articles, standard operating procedures and support documentation.
- Provide practical guidance and training that helps users make effective and secure use of technology.

OUTCOME 5: IT records, controls and evidence are complete, current and audit-ready 
- Maintain complete and accurate asset, software, licence, supplier and other operational IT registers.
- Record equipment allocation, ownership, status, location, lifecycle and disposal information, and perform periodic reconciliations.
- Follow and help maintain IT policies, standards, procedures and control evidence.
- Complete routine operational checks and scheduled control activities, escalating risks, exceptions or control failures promptly.
- Support audits, reviews and compliance activities by providing accurate records and evidence.
- Handle devices, accounts and information in line with security, privacy and records-management requirements.
- Support compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 (as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025), including immediately escalating any suspected personal data breach to the Data Protection Lead so that the organisation can meet the 72-hour ICO reporting deadline where applicable.

OUTCOME 6: Small projects and improvements are delivered and technology keeps getting better 
- Deliver or support small IT projects, upgrades, application roll-outs and service improvements.
- Gather requirements, coordinate suppliers, plan user communications, support testing and manage implementation activities.
- Identify opportunities to improve reliability, security, efficiency and the user experience.
- Keep project actions, risks, decisions, documentation and handover materials up to date.

Success Measures Success in the role will be assessed through:

Service delivery 
- Users receive dependable and responsive first and second-line technical support, with routine and complex issues resolved effectively.
- Incidents and requests are responded to and resolved within agreed service levels.
- User satisfaction with IT support is consistently positive.
Accuracy, security and control 
- Incidents, requests, access changes and joiner, mover and leaver activities are completed accurately and on time.
- 100% of leaver accounts disabled by the end of the last working day; new joiners fully equipped and set up on day one.
- Operational records, registers and control evidence are complete, current and reliable.
- Periodic access reviews and asset reconciliations completed on schedule with no significant audit findings.
Change and improvement 
- Changes and small projects are delivered in a controlled way with minimal disruption.
- Recurring problems are reduced and practical improvements are implemented continuously.
- Feedback from the Senior IT Manager, colleagues and suppliers on collaboration, communication and ownership.

Technical Expertise & Role-Specific Capability Essential 
- Strong hands-on experience providing both first and second-line IT support within a modern workplace environment, with particular strength in diagnosing and resolving more complex technical issues.
- Demonstrable experience managing a broad range of incidents and service requests through their full lifecycle, from initial user contact to resolution.
- Practical experience of joiner, mover and leaver processes, identity administration, permissions and access control.
- Experience administering Microsoft 365 and supporting Windows devices, laptops, mobile devices and common business applications.
- Experience maintaining IT asset records, operational registers, procedures and control evidence.
- Understanding of proportionate change management, information security and data protection practices.
- Ability to troubleshoot methodically, make sound decisions and know when to engage specialist support.
- Experience coordinating external IT suppliers and seeing actions through to completion.
- Ability to organise a varied workload independently and balance urgent support needs with planned operational work.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical matters to non-technical users.
- Experience contributing to or delivering small IT projects and technology changes.

Desirable 
- Experience in a small organisation where the role covers a broad range of operational IT responsibilities.
- Working knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, Autopilot, SharePoint and Teams administration.
- Experience with IT service management tools and ITIL-aligned working practices.

- Technically credible, user-focused and committed to providing a high-quality service.
DELIVER — Driving outcomes and execution
- Proactive and self-sufficient, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.

Our flagship mobile product, Fanatics Live , is where that experience comes to life: live card breaks, real-time auctions, high-traffic chat, marketplace transactions, and deep collection management tools. The iOS stack is modern by design. We're SwiftUI-first, run The Composable Architecture TCA) across the app, use Swift Concurrency throughout, talk to our backend via Apollo GraphQL, and maintain a clean modular SPM codebase generated with Tuist. There's no legacy UIKit app hiding under the surface — you'll be working in a codebase you can be proud of.

AI tooling is part of how we work. We expect engineers to use it on the job, give it good context, and verify the output — not just accept it.

- Design and ship production iOS features across the live-break experience: auctions, stream viewing, chat, marketplace, and collector tools

- Write genuine test coverage: unit tests with mock dependencies, TCA

- TestStore assertions, async test patterns — not coverage theater

- Contribute to architectural decisions: modularization strategy, effect management, failure handling

- Mentor engineers earlier in their career and raise the quality bar across the team
